title: Light
hookLine: a square of late sun slides across the wall. it was behind every color this week.
tomorrow: what can you see through an empty window?

lines: A SQUARE OF SUN ON THE WALL.
THE NEXT DISC IS LIGHT ITSELF.
cards: Late afternoon, a square of sun slides slowly across a bedroom wall. It's easy to miss; it's just there. Yesterday asked what a patch of sun on a wall has to do with any of this.
Here's the answer: everything this week needed it. In the dark, no flame shows and no blue or red is a color at all. So Buddhaghosa's next disc is the light itself.
Sunlight or moonlight coming through a gap in a wall or a window, making a circle on the wall or floor. Or light falling through the leaves of a thick tree.
Or a lamp set inside a pot, shining out through a hole in its side.

teach.b: The note is simple: light, light. At first the image looks like that circle on the wall. Later, the manual says, it becomes a bright, compact glow.

Notice the fire's trick again: a gap in the wall does the framing, the way the hole in the mat did. And since today looks back, hold the week up to it. A flame, framed, with the sticks and smoke left outside.
Wind, never seen, known by the leaves it moves. Blue, and an old argument: calm first, insight first, or both yoked together. Yellow, just the seen, before the story arrives.
Red, and a fine peg to knock out an angry thought.
White, and a mind called luminous.

teach.h: ONE THING, PLAINLY WHAT IT IS.
teach.b: Seven objects, one thread through all of them: choose one thing, let it be plainly what it is, and rest there until the mind steadies.
Light makes a fitting end to the week, because it was there the whole time, behind every other color.

how: In Theravada meditation the light kasina uses sunlight or moonlight cast as a circle on a wall or floor, or lamplight through a hole, noted as 'light, light', as the Visuddhimagga describes; it is taken up with a teacher.

o: a lamp lit at a shrine to honor the Buddha each night
a circle of light on a wall, used as a meditation object
the bright flash said to come at the moment of awakening

games.q: how to make a disc of light — tap the pairs.
p: a circle of light on the wall

s: the light disc can be made from sunlight through a gap in a wall
or light through thick leaves, or a lamp inside a pot with a hole in its side.
each color disc has a hidden symbolic meaning to decode
the instruction is the plain color, named plainly: blue, blue; red, red.
in the luminous-mind teaching, stains are the mind's own color
they come in like visitors; the mind itself is called luminous.

games.q: your little brother asks what you've been staring at all week. what's the best one-line answer?
o: one thing at a time, seen plainly, until the mind settles.
colors that each hide a secret meaning you have to decode.
anything at all; what you look at doesn't really matter.
games.why: each disc is plain: fire as fire, red as red. Buddhaghosa is careful about each object, but there's no secret code. just one thing, seen plainly.

practice: Find where light lands in your room: a window's square on the wall, a lamp's glow, sun on the floor. Rest your eyes on the brightness itself rather than the wall under it. When the mind drifts, note light, light, and come back.

wordCard.voice: Light: aloka in Pali. A circle of sun or lamplight on a wall, the disc every other color needed.

orig.note: Pali: light. The disc of sun or lamplight, held in mind with the plain word, light, light.

carryVoice: Your line: light on the wall. It was behind every color this week. That's a week of discs.

sources.ref: Visuddhimagga 5 (the light kasina: sunlight or moonlight entering through a hole in a wall or a window and cast as a circle on wall or floor, or through the leaves of a dense tree, or a lamp in a pot shining through a hole; noted as 'light, light'; the learning sign like the circle, the counterpart sign a compact, bright cluster of light)
